Parties: we represent Meridian Fieldworks, Inc.; counterparty is Copperleaf Technology Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Finding submitted.

**Summary:** § 19.2 was a material deviation — it limited the Deliverable/software conformance warranty to fifteen days and cut off any correction or refund obligation thereafter, well below the 90-day fallback floor. The supporting provisions were already adequate: § 19.1 carries untimed professional/workmanlike and conformance warranties (Services include hosted software), § 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance and malicious code, § 19.4 supplies re-perform/repair/replace plus a refund of Fees paid, and § 19.5 expressly preserves the express warranties against the disclaimer.

**Redline:** one surgical change — "For fifteen days after delivery" → "For ninety days after delivery" — bringing the clause to the fallback position without disturbing any other language.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.","status":"already_met","quote":"Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications."},{"element":"Services are warranted for at least 30 days.","status":"already_met","quote":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."},{"element":"Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.","status":"already_met","quote":"Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."},{"element":"Warranty remedies include a refund.","status":"already_met","quote":"Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."}]}

Finding rationale:
The fallback elements are supplied by §§ 19.1 and 19.4: § 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance and untimed material conformance of Services (defined in § 1.7 to include the hosted software) and Deliverables to their documentation, and § 19.4 gives re-performance/repair/replacement plus a refund of Fees paid. The deviation is § 19.2, which fixed a fifteen-day conformance period for Deliverables and then extinguished any correction or refund obligation after that date — below the 90-day floor and, as drafted with an unqualified cut-off read together with § 19.4's reference to "Section 19.1 or 19.2", capable of being argued to cut off correction and refund obligations generally (including for the hosted software warranted in § 19.1). Our single operation extends the period to ninety (90) days and scopes the cut-off to that Deliverable, leaving §§ 19.1, 19.3 and 19.4 verbatim. Preferred-level points we note but do not redline: no express 12-month software conformance period, and § 19.3's malicious-code warranty is narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" (§ 19.3 does carry the Applicable Law compliance warranty).

elements.evidence: § 19.3 is not rendered; the drafter reports it is narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which would fall short of an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty, but the operative text is unavailable for inspection.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the rendered language: the 15-day Deliverable conformance period is raised to ninety (90) days, the untimed § 19.1 Services/hosted-software conformance warranty survives, and § 19.4's repair/replace plus refund remedies are retained verbatim.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only § 19.2 — a numeric change from fifteen to ninety days plus the three-word scoping phrase "for that Deliverable". The scoping is not cosmetic: without it the unqualified cut-off, cross-referenced by § 19.4 ("Section 19.1 or 19.2"), is a contradictory retained sentence that could be argued to extinguish correction and refund obligations for the § 19.1 Services/hosted-software warranties that supply fallback elements 1 and 2. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added.

Intent is preserved: § 19.4's cross-reference to Sections 19.1 and 19.2 remains accurate, the non-exclusive-remedy carve-outs for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims are untouched, and no defined term is left dangling.

Per the playbook these are rationale notes, not separate deviations.

[{"id":"f-indemn-24c442f6","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 20 INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.","rationale":"Section 20 contains a single, one-way Customer indemnity covering \"every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services\", and there is no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement (searches for indemnity/infringement return only §§ 9.3, 19.4-19.5, 21.3 and 29.2, none of which create a Vendor indemnity). That is walk-away territory: no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services. We therefore insert the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity (IP infringement of the Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a notice/control/cooperation procedure, and narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law. Note also that § 9.3 cross-refers to \"the remedies required by Section 20.5\", which does not exist; if Vendor prefers the fallback (IP indemnity with customary modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x annual fee super-cap), that dangling reference should be filled at the same time.","proposal":"Add Vendor defence/indemnity for IP, legal breach, data breach and wilful misconduct with claim procedure, and narrow Customer's indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-2cd5008c","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","rationale":"The IP package meets our preferred position, not merely the fallback. Section 14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for it and contains an express present assignment by Vendor of all worldwide right, title, and interest (plus equivalent assignments from Vendor personnel). Section 14.3 confines Vendor's retained rights to \"Vendor Technology,\" defined in Section 1.8 as Vendor's pre-existing technology and expressly excluding Customer Data and IP Customer owned before the Effective Date, and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the Section 13.2 licence back, which is \"perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid\" to use, modify, create derivative works from and permit contractors to support for Customer's business — covering the perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free elements. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data and Customer-provided material, and the only right passing to Vendor is the limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer, which is service delivery rather than independent exploitation; Section 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data commingling and model training absent our express written consent (a consent gate, not a standing licence). Section 14.4 creates no jointly owned IP unless both Parties sign a separate instrument identifying exploitation rights, which we control. No provision assigns Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor, so there is no walk-away exposure. Two adjacent points are noted only, not redlined here: Section 13.1's revocable, non-transferable Services licence excluding Affiliates and contractors is a Services-access problem for the LICENSE rule (and is partly answered by Section 13.3), and Section 11.1's immediate deletion language is a TRANSITION issue; neither dilutes the ownership and Customer Data direction this rule tests, and we do not flag the same term twice.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-c4f0f7cf","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to an M&A/asset-sale successor without Vendor's consent (Affiliate is broadly defined at 1.1 by >50% control or power to direct management); 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, subject only to a reasonableness standard, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor; 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control. Section 13.3 reinforces our licence-transfer right on a permitted assignment. Only minor sub-elements fall short of ideal wording — the competitor bar is framed as \"without Customer's consent\" rather than absolute, and the reasonableness qualifier in 24.2 is keyed to an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing — which we note but do not redline given consent is required for every Vendor assignment in any event. No walk-away features (no blanket bar on Customer assignment, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right) are present.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-75577550","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"Section 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery failures — full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback on every material term. Section 12.3 states we have made \"no exclusivity ... commitment\", but that is an internal conflict rather than a cure, and the Section 2.2 order-of-precedence clause does not resolve conflicts within the Agreement itself. We therefore take the preferred position and convert Section 2.2 to a non-exclusive appointment, which also aligns it with Section 12.3. The separate take-or-pay minimum commitment in Section 2.1 is a volume, not an exclusivity, term and is addressed under its own rule.","proposal":"Make Vendor a non-exclusive provider in Section 2.2","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-549be92f","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated\", \"penalty\", \"early termination fee\", acceleration and shortfall language return no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty anywhere in the Agreement. The termination architecture affirmatively confirms the preferred position: § 9.4 limits Customer's exposure on convenience termination to Fees for conforming Services rendered through the effective date with a refund of prepaid Fees; § 27.3 permits termination for prolonged force majeure \"without penalty\"; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; and § 21.3 treats Customer's payment of undisputed Fees as a debt rather than damages. No early-termination fee mechanic exists, so the fallback cap is unnecessary. The take-or-pay minimum in § 2.1 is a volume commitment rather than a stipulated damages amount and is addressed under MINCOMMIT; we do not flag it twice here. This clause set meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-8dd04f65","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.","rationale":"Section 13.1 grants the Services licence to \"Customer alone\", expressly \"without Affiliates or contractors\", and makes it \"revocable at Vendor's sole discretion\" — walk-away territory: affiliates and contractors are excluded with no path to add them (the defined \"Customer\" is Meridian Fieldworks alone and does not include Affiliates), and the licence is revocable at will. This fails even the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice) and contradicts the retained revocation limit in 13.3. The reconciling provisions already deliver the remaining preferred elements: 13.2 gives a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence to Customer and its Affiliates, and 13.3 (with 24.1) permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor. Our single edit to 13.1 extends the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and replaces discretionary revocation with termination only for uncured material breach; deleting \"non-transferable\" also removes the conflict with the 13.3 transfer right.","proposal":"Extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove Vendor's discretionary revocation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-768576ee","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"Section 12.4 binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete (\"any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory\") running 24 months past the term — walk-away territory under this rule (post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, undefined scope) — and it contradicts the pro-Customer confirmation in Section 12.3. No other clause imposes a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer (Section 13.4 is ordinary use restrictions; Section 2.2 exclusivity is a separate rule; Section 24.2 binds Vendor). We take the preferred position by striking the offending sentence as intentionally omitted, relying on the retained Section 12.3 confirmation rather than restating the same permission twice; the narrowed fallback is offered in the comment only.","proposal":"Strike the 24-month post-term non-compete in Section 12.4 as intentionally omitted, relying on Section 12.3.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-t4c-a8bfaeb9","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches, and a document-wide review of the termination provisions (§§ 9.1–9.5, 8.2–8.3, 27.3, 24.4) shows no Vendor right to terminate without cause; § 8.2 non-renewal is Customer-side only and in any event belongs under RENEWAL. The one tension is § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment \"without reduction or termination rights\", which cuts against the § 9.4 exit economics; that is the minimum-commitment bargain and is addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than flagged twice here. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-3e7ce3f7","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.","rationale":"Section 11.1 is walk-away territory: it requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, and it contradicts 11.2 (30-day machine-readable return) and 11.3 (deletion and written certification after confirmed return). The Agreement contains no transition assistance period anywhere (10.1 merely refers to \"any agreed transition period\"), so the fallback 90 days of assistance is also unmet, and 11.2's return runs from Customer's request rather than expiry or termination. Because the machine-readable format and post-return certified deletion elements are already met in 11.2 and 11.3, we target the preferred level with two surgical edits: 11.1 becomes up to six months of assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, and 11.2's 30-day return is anchored to expiry or termination (retaining the request trigger and all other wording verbatim).","proposal":"Replace immediate cessation/deletion in 11.1 with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, and anchor the 30-day data return to expiry or termination.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-ff057a57","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 is the only audit right binding Customer (Section 23 contains no operative assurance obligation, and no other verification, inspection or remote-monitoring right appears in the document). It meets every element of our preferred position: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, off-site where practicable, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§ 22.1); Vendor bears costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly (§ 22.2). Section 22.3 further protects us by making findings Customer Confidential Information. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-dae1813e","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"The clause sits at our preferred position. Section 28.1 applies New York law to the Agreement and each dispute arising from it, and Section 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County, New York exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a waiver of venue/forum objections. The only carve-out is the customary right to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. A search of the document found no arbitration provision, so there is no foreign seat. The pre-suit executive escalation in Section 28.3 expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-preserving filings, so it does not impair the forum. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-161552fc","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or most-favoured-customer obligation running from Customer to Vendor. Section 12.3 expressly confirms Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, and there is no disclosure, benchmarking, or right-to-match mechanic anywhere (searches for \"most-favoured\", \"favourable/favorable\", \"match\", \"first refusal\", and benchmarking language returned nothing else). The pricing provisions run the other way in our favour: § 7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term and bars unstated charges, and § 8.3 caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and three percent, both obligations on Vendor only. It also contradicts § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer \"has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment\") and undercuts our § 9.4 convenience-termination right. No other clause supplies a reduction, exit, or true-up mechanic: § 7.1 only fixes Fees per Order Form and the § 22.2-22.3 shortfall language relates to usage audits, not to this commitment. We therefore redline § 2.1 to the fallback with a single surgical replacement, leaving the rest of the payment architecture intact.","proposal":"Narrow § 2.1 take-or-pay to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of a penalty.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-9ac0f612","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"Renewal terms meet our preferred position in full: automatic renewals are limited to successive twelve-month periods (§ 8.2), Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (within the 30-day maximum), Vendor must send a renewal reminder at least sixty days before renewal (with Customer's opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is additional protection for us), and renewal uplifts are capped at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent (§ 8.3), plus ninety days' notice of any increase and no increase on prepaid periods. No multi-year automatic renewal or long non-renewal window appears anywhere in the document, so no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-8378d88a","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.","rationale":"The fallback elements are supplied by §§ 19.1 and 19.4: § 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance and untimed material conformance of Services (defined in § 1.7 to include the hosted software) and Deliverables to their documentation, and § 19.4 gives re-performance/repair/replacement plus a refund of Fees paid. The deviation is § 19.2, which fixed a fifteen-day conformance period for Deliverables and then extinguished any correction or refund obligation after that date — below the 90-day floor and, as drafted with an unqualified cut-off read together with § 19.4's reference to \"Section 19.1 or 19.2\", capable of being argued to cut off correction and refund obligations generally (including for the hosted software warranted in § 19.1). Our single operation extends the period to ninety (90) days and scopes the cut-off to that Deliverable, leaving §§ 19.1, 19.3 and 19.4 verbatim. Preferred-level points we note but do not redline: no express 12-month software conformance period, and § 19.3's malicious-code warranty is narrowed to code \"intentionally introduced by Vendor\" (§ 19.3 does carry the Applicable Law compliance warranty).","proposal":"Extend § 19.2 from fifteen to ninety (90) days and scope the post-period cut-off to that Deliverable.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-32e72a01","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","rationale":"Section 18 meets the preferred position in full: CGL at USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, professional E&O at USD 2,000,000, cyber and privacy liability at USD 5,000,000 (granted unconditionally, so the Customer Data-processing trigger is satisfied; Customer Data is broadly defined at 1.3), workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates of insurance on request under 18.2. The clause adds further Customer-favourable terms (employer's liability, a one-year tail, primary coverage, notice of cancellation, and non-limitation of Vendor's liabilities). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-99743d6a","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.","rationale":"Section 21.1 caps each Party's aggregate liability at one month of Fees and does so \"without exception\", which is below the fallback 12-month basis (and below our 6-month walk-away floor) and overrides the Excluded Claims defined in 21.3, leaving indemnification, confidentiality/data-protection, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap with no super-cap. The single replace to 21.1 sets a mutual twelve (12) months' Fees cap expressly subject to Excluded Claims, which 21.3 defines to include indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct, so every fallback element is met in operative language. Preferred is not reached: the cap retains \"actually paid\" with no USD 1,000,000 floor, and the 21.3 payment carve-out is limited to \"undisputed Fees for conforming Services\", which under the s.1.5 Fees definition does not exempt Customer's payment obligations generally; these are noted rather than pursued. Favourable retained language in 21.2 (mutual exclusion of indirect damages, direct-damages characterisation) and 21.3 is untouched, and 21.2 already referenced Excluded Claims so no dangling term is created.","proposal":"Cap raised to 12 months' Fees and Excluded Claims placed outside the mutual cap","verification":"repaired"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. Of the eighteen rules tested, eleven clauses are compliant (several at our preferred position, not merely the fallback) and seven are deviations requiring redlines. Six of the seven deviations are material enough to sit in walk-away territory as currently drafted.

The critical issue is indemnification: § 20 contains a one-way Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", and there is no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement. This is compounded by § 21.1, which caps each Party's liability at one month of Fees "without exception", overriding the Excluded Claims that § 21.3 already defines.

Three clauses impose competitive and volume restraints that our playbook does not accept: full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2), a 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope (§ 12.4), and a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment stripped of any reduction or termination right (§ 2.1). Notably, each of these contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We are relying on § 12.3 as drafting support, but internal inconsistency is not a cure and the § 2.2 order-of-precedence clause does not resolve conflicts within the Agreement itself.

Two further deviations are narrower: § 13.1 grants the Services licence to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors and making the licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion (contradicting §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 24.1); and § 11.1 requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data (contradicting §§ 11.2 and 11.3). § 19.2's fifteen-day Deliverable warranty is below our floor and, as drafted, arguably cuts off correction and refund obligations generally.

On the credit side, the IP and Customer Data package (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4, 15.1), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), renewal and price uplift (§§ 8.2–8.3), audit (§ 22), insurance (§ 18), governing law and venue (§ 28) all meet our preferred position, and there are no Customer-payable liquidated damages, MFN or non-solicitation obligations anywhere in the document.

One housekeeping point: § 9.3 cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist. That dangling reference should be resolved as part of the indemnity negotiation.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 20 (esp. 20.1); cf. §§ 9.3, 19.4–19.5, 21.3, 29.2 | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity anywhere. Walk-away. Insert Vendor defence/indemnity (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice/control/cooperation procedure, and narrow our indemnity. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4, 15.1, 1.8 | Preferred position met: present assignment of Deliverables, Vendor retained rights confined to Vendor Technology, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence back, Customer owns Customer Data with processing-only rights for Vendor. No redline. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2; cf. § 12.3 | Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full term, no category limit, no 12-month cap, no performance-based exit. Walk-away; fails fallback on every material term. Convert to non-exclusive. |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4; cf. § 12.3 | 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"). Walk-away. Strike as intentionally omitted, relying on § 12.3. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1; cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3, 24.1 | Licence to "Customer alone", expressly excluding Affiliates and contractors, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Walk-away; fails fallback. Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; revocation only for uncured material breach; delete "non-transferable". |
| 6 | High | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1; cf. §§ 11.2, 11.3, 10.1 | Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data, no export or migration support; no transition period anywhere. Walk-away. Replace with up to six months' assistance at then-current rates; anchor § 11.2's 30-day return to expiry or termination. |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3, 1.1 | Preferred position met: Customer free to assign to Affiliate/successor; Vendor assignment and change of control require our consent; no Vendor termination, repricing or acceleration on our change of control. Minor wording points noted only. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4; cf. §§ 9.1–9.5, 8.2–8.3, 27.3, 24.4 | Preferred position met: 30 days' notice, whole or partial, refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. Tension with § 2.1 take-or-pay is addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 9 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4; cf. §§ 27.3, 7.3, 21.3 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or acceleration anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1; cf. §§ 12.3, 9.4, 7.1, 22.2–22.3 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Walk-away; short of fallback. Narrow to current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, shortfall handled by true-up. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2; cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 1.7 | Fifteen-day Deliverable conformance period with an unqualified post-period cut-off of correction and refund obligations; below the 90-day floor and arguably cuts off § 19.1 remedies. Extend to 90 days and scope the cut-off to that Deliverable. |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 | Preferred position met: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears costs absent >5% underpayment, no direct system access. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state and federal courts; no arbitration provision; customary injunctive-relief carve-out only. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12.3; cf. §§ 7.1, 8.3 | No MFN/MFC, benchmarking or right-to-match obligation; § 12.3 expressly confirms none. Pricing obligations run in our favour. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No solicitation, no-hire or inducement covenant on Customer; § 12.3 preserves general-recruitment hiring. § 12.4 is addressed under NONCOMPETE. |
